title: Overhaul securities laws with a simpler, three-tier disclosure system
proposal: The chapter says the SEC and Congress should fundamentally rewrite securities laws, creating a simpler disclosure system with three categories of firms (private, smaller, and public) and disclosure rules scaled to size.
quote: The SEC and Congress should fundamentally reform the securities laws

title: Abolish PCAOB and FINRA and merge their work into the SEC
proposal: The chapter recommends abolishing the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board and the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority and moving their regulatory duties into the SEC.
quote: PCAOB and FINRA should be abolished, and their regulatory functions should be merged into the SEC.

title: Create a commission to study moving other self-regulators into SEC
proposal: The chapter says Congress should set up an independent board or commission to report within 18 months on whether the duties of other "self-regulatory organizations" should move to the SEC.
quote: and charge it with producing a detailed report within 18 months that examines the degree to which the regulatory functions

title: Abolish DEI offices at financial regulators
proposal: The chapter says offices at financial regulators that promote "diversity, equity, and inclusion," which it describes as racist policies, should be abolished, and rules requiring appointments based on race, ethnicity, sex, or sexual orientation should be eliminated.
quote: Offices at financial regulators that promote racist policies (usually in the name of "diversity, equity, and inclusion") should be abolished

title: Use SEC exemption power more to ease rules on small issuers
proposal: The chapter says the SEC should use its broad "general exemptive authority" much more often to reduce regulatory burdens on companies raising money, especially smaller entrepreneurs.
quote: It should use this authority significantly more often to reduce the regulatory burden on issuers, particularly smaller entrepreneurs.

title: Simplify Regulation A and crowdfunding; preempt state registration
proposal: The chapter says the SEC should simplify Regulation A (small offerings) and Regulation CF (crowdfunding) and override state "blue sky" registration requirements for Regulation A offerings.
quote: Simplify and streamline Regulation A (the small issues exemption)12 and Regulation CF (crowdfunding)13 and preempt blue sky registration

title: Broaden or eliminate the "accredited investor" limit
proposal: The chapter says the SEC should let more people invest in private offerings, either by widening the definition of "accredited investor" or by removing that restriction entirely.
quote: Either democratize access to private offerings by broadening the definition of accredited investor for purposes of Regulation D or eliminate the accredited investor restriction altogether.

title: Allow investors to self-certify accredited status
proposal: The chapter says investors should be allowed to certify their own accredited investor status for all Regulation D Rule 506 offerings.
quote: Allow traditional self-certification of accredited investor status for all Regulation D Rule 506 offerings.

title: Exempt small micro-offerings from SEC registration
proposal: The chapter says very small securities offerings should be exempt from registration requirements.
quote: Exempt small micro-offerings from registration requirements.

title: Exempt small "finders" from broker-dealer registration
proposal: The chapter says small and occasional "finders" who connect businesses with investors should not have to register as broker-dealers, and private placement brokers should get a simpler registration process.
quote: Exempt small and intermittent finders from broker–dealer registration requirements and provide a simplified registration process for private placement brokers.

title: Exempt peer-to-peer lending from securities laws
proposal: The chapter says peer-to-peer lending should be exempt from federal and state securities laws, and rules on crowdfunding debt should be eased.
quote: Exempt peer-to-peer lending from federal and state securities laws and reduce the regulatory burden on Regulation CF debt securities.

title: Make Emerging Growth Company exemptions permanent
proposal: The chapter says the reduced rules for "Emerging Growth Companies" under Title I of the JOBS Act should be made permanent for all such companies.
quote: Make the Title I Emerging Growth Company (EGC) exemptions permanent for all EGCs.

title: Ease rules for small broker-dealers, including audit requirements
proposal: The chapter says the SEC should reduce rules on small broker-dealers and exempt privately held firms that do not hold customer assets from having to use PCAOB-registered auditors.
quote: Reduce the regulatory burden on small broker–dealers and exempt privately held, non-custodial broker–dealers from the requirements to use a PCAOB-

title: Don't count crowdfunding investors toward S-corp shareholder limit
proposal: The chapter says Congress should change the tax code so crowdfunding and Regulation A investors do not count toward the 100-shareholder limit for S corporations.
quote: Amend the Internal Revenue Code to disregard crowdfunding and Regulation A shareholders for purposes of the 100-shareholder limit for Subchapter S corporations.

title: Preempt state rules for securities traded on established markets
proposal: The chapter says the SEC should override state "blue sky" registration and reporting rules for securities traded on established markets such as national exchanges.
quote: Preempt blue sky registration, qualification, and continuing reporting requirements for securities traded on established securities markets

title: End the Consolidated Audit Trail (CAT) program
proposal: The chapter recommends ending the Consolidated Audit Trail, an SEC system that tracks trading activity in U.S. stock and options markets.
quote: Terminate the Consolidated Audit Trail (CAT) program.

title: Abolish Rule 144 limits on reselling securities
proposal: The chapter says Rule 144 and similar limits on reselling securities should be abolished. Instead, companies that sold securities would have to provide enough current information for buyers to make reasonable decisions.
quote: Abolish Rule 144 and other regulations that restrict securities resales

title: Bar SEC from requiring non-financial social or climate disclosures
proposal: The chapter says Congress should forbid the SEC from requiring companies to disclose social, political, or "human capital" information that is not material to investors' financial risks or returns. It singles out the proposed SEC climate disclosure rule.
quote: Prohibit the SEC from requiring issuer disclosure of social, ideological, political, or "human capital" information that is not material to investors'

title: Repeal Dodd-Frank disclosures on conflict minerals and CEO pay ratio
proposal: The chapter says Congress should repeal disclosure rules required by the Dodd-Frank Act on conflict minerals, mine safety, resource extraction payments, and the ratio of CEO pay to worker pay.
quote: Repeal the Dodd–Frank mandated disclosures relating to conflict minerals, mine safety, resource extraction, and CEO pay ratios.

title: Forbid securities regulators from race- or sex-based rules
proposal: The chapter says Congress should bar securities regulators, including self-regulatory bodies, from making rules or taking actions that treat people differently based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin, favorably or unfavorably.
quote: Prohibit securities regulators, including SROs, from promulgating rules or taking other actions that discriminate, either favorably or unfavorably

title: Publish an annual SEC data book
proposal: The chapter says the SEC should publish better data on securities offerings, markets, and enforcement, including an annual data book of trends over time.
quote: Publish better data on securities offerings, securities markets, and securities law enforcement and publish an annual data book of time series data

title: Let any three SEC Commissioners set agenda items
proposal: The chapter says any three SEC Commissioners should be able to put an item on the agenda and get staff support, even without the Chairman's backing.
quote: Ensure that any three SEC Commissioners are empowered to place an item on the agenda and to receive adequate staff support

title: End SEC in-house administrative trials
proposal: The chapter says the SEC should eliminate nearly all of its in-house administrative proceedings, or at least let accused parties choose a regular federal court instead.
quote: Eliminate all administrative proceedings (APs) within the SEC except for stop orders related to defective registration statements.

title: Stop delegating SEC decisions to open enforcement cases
proposal: The chapter says the SEC should stop letting staff decide on their own to start enforcement cases, and study whether other staff powers should be narrowed or set to expire.
quote: End the practice of delegating the decision to initiate an enforcement case.

title: Require a watchdog report on SEC tech spending
proposal: The chapter says Congress should require an Inspector General or GAO report on SEC information technology spending and contracting, which it calls too high and poorly managed.
quote: Require an Inspector General's (or possibly a GAO) report regarding SEC information technology spending and contracting.

title: Limit SEC investigations to two years
proposal: The chapter says Congress should limit SEC investigations by law to two years, with no extensions.
quote: Statutorily limit the time for an investigation to two years with no extensions.

title: Streamline SEC management: fewer managers and merged offices
proposal: The chapter says the SEC Chairman should sharply cut the number of officials reporting directly to the Chairman, merge offices doing similar work, and reduce the number of managers per employee.
quote: Dramatically reduce the number of direct reports to the SEC Chairman.

title: Update the legal definition of "commodity"
proposal: The chapter says Congress should modernize the definition of commodity, which it says is mostly a list of farm products, and clarify how digital assets are treated.
quote: Modernize the definition of commodity (which is now largely a laundry list of agricultural commodities)25 and clarify the treatment of digital assets.

title: Clarify when foreign swap platforms must register with CFTC
proposal: The chapter says Congress should amend the Commodity Exchange Act to make clear when a foreign swap trading platform must register with the CFTC.
quote: Clarify through an express amendment to the Commodity Exchange Act (CEA)26 the circumstances that require a foreign swap trading platform to

title: Let the CFTC Chairman remove the Executive Director
proposal: The chapter says the Commodity Exchange Act should be changed so the CFTC Chairman can remove the agency's Executive Director without a Commission vote.
quote: Amend Section 2 of the CEA to authorize the CFTC Chairman to remove the agency's Executive Director without a Commission vote.

title: Set CFTC Commissioners' office budgets by law
proposal: The chapter says Congress should set funding for each CFTC Commissioner's office in law, adjusted for inflation, so Commissioners don't need the Chairman's approval for budgets.
quote: establish funding amounts for the Commissioners' offices by statute with adjustments for inflation

title: Replace CFTC position limits rule with exchange-set limits
proposal: The chapter says the CFTC should replace its rule limiting the size of traders' positions with more authority for exchanges to set their own limits where appropriate.
quote: Replace the existing position limits rule, which reduces liquidity and makes markets more volatile, with further delegation of authority to the exchanges

title: Reduce overly detailed CFTC rules
proposal: The chapter says the CFTC should cut back overly prescriptive rules that implement its core principles and put more resources into core functions.
quote: Reduce overly prescriptive rules implementing the CFTC's core principles.

title: Align CFTC cross-border swap definitions with the 2020 rule
proposal: The chapter says the CFTC should use the 2020 rule's definitions of "U.S. Person" and "Guarantee" for requirements still covered by older 2013 guidance, so the terms are consistent.
quote: Apply the definitions of "U.S. Person" and "Guarantee" in the CFTC's 2020 rule on cross-border application of swaps regulations

title: Drop two confusing CFTC cross-border categories
proposal: The chapter says the CFTC should remove the "affiliate conduit" and "foreign consolidated subsidiary" categories from its older cross-border guidance and margin rule.
quote: Remove the regulatory categories of "affiliate conduit" and "foreign consolidated subsidiary" from the 2013 Guidance

title: Joint SEC-CFTC rule treating most crypto as commodities
proposal: The chapter says the SEC and CFTC should issue a joint rule saying most digital tokens are commodities regulated by the CFTC unless holders get a share of profits or rights to a company's assets. If regulators don't act, Congress should pass a law.
quote: Promulgate a joint regulation providing that a holder of digital assets may not be deemed a party to an investment contract

title: Treat commodity-backed certificates as commodities, not securities
proposal: The chapter says definitions should be changed so non-security digital assets count as commodities, and certificates that can be traded for a physical commodity on demand are commodities, not securities.
quote: Amend the definition of commodity to include digital assets that are not a security as so defined

title: Open FINRA board meetings and hearings to the public
proposal: If FINRA is not merged into the SEC, the chapter says its board meetings, agendas, minutes, planned rules, and arbitration and disciplinary hearings should be open or published.
quote: FINRA's Board of Governors meetings be open to the public unless the board votes to meet in executive session.

title: Require written findings in FINRA arbitration decisions
proposal: The chapter says FINRA arbitrators should have to explain their awards with findings of fact, and these decisions should be open to SEC review and limited court review.
quote: Require FINRA arbitrators to make findings of fact based on the evidentiary record and demonstrate how those facts led to the award given

title: Send self-regulator fines to investors or the Treasury
proposal: The chapter says fines imposed by self-regulatory organizations like FINRA should go to a new investor reimbursement fund or the Treasury, so these groups have no financial interest in fines.
quote: Require that all SRO fines, including those imposed by FINRA, should go either to a newly established investor reimbursement fund or to the Treasury.

title: Require cost-benefit analysis for self-regulator rules
proposal: The chapter says all self-regulatory organizations should do meaningful cost-benefit analysis when making major rules.
quote: Require all SROs to conduct meaningful cost-benefit analysis as part of the rulemaking process with respect to major rules.

title: Require public comment on self-regulator rules
proposal: The chapter says self-regulatory organizations should publish proposed rules and ask for public comment before sending them to the SEC or CFTC.
quote: Require all SROs to publish rules in proposed format and seek public comment before they are submitted to the SEC or the CFTC.

title: Require annual self-regulator reports to Congress
proposal: The chapter says each self-regulatory organization should file a detailed annual report to Congress on its budget, fees, enforcement, dispute resolution, and rulemaking.
quote: Require each SRO to submit an annual report to Congress with detailed, specified information about its budget and fees

title: Hold annual congressional hearings on self-regulators
proposal: The chapter says Congress should hold oversight hearings on self-regulatory organizations every year.
quote: Conduct annual oversight hearings on SROs.

title: Put FINRA, MSRB, and NFA under an inspector general
proposal: The chapter says Congress should place FINRA, the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board, and the National Futures Association under an inspector general, either a new one or an existing one.
quote: establish an inspector general with respect to financial SROs, including FINRA, the MSRB, and the NFA

title: Require SEC and CFTC annual reports on self-regulator oversight
proposal: The chapter says Congress should require the SEC and CFTC to publish a detailed annual report on how they supervise self-regulatory organizations.
quote: Require the SEC and the CFTC to publish a detailed annual report on SRO supervision.

title: Abolish the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau
proposal: The chapter says Congress should abolish the CFPB and return its consumer protection duties to banking regulators and the Federal Trade Commission.
quote: Congress should abolish the CFPB and reverse Dodd–Frank Section 1061, thus returning the consumer protection function of the CFPB to banking regulators

title: Order CFPB dissolution if the Supreme Court rules its funding invalid
proposal: The chapter says that if the Supreme Court upheld the Fifth Circuit ruling against the CFPB's funding, the President should order the agency dissolved, withdraw its rules and guidance, and send its staff back to their former agencies.
quote: the next conservative President should order the immediate dissolution of the agency

title: Send unused CFPB penalty money to the Treasury
proposal: Until the CFPB is abolished, the chapter says Congress should require that civil penalty money not used to repay harmed consumers go to the Treasury instead of being spent at the Director's discretion.
quote: Ensure that any civil penalty funds not used to recompense wronged consumers go to the Department of the Treasury.

title: Repeal the Dodd-Frank small-business lending data rule (Sec. 1071)
proposal: The chapter says Congress should repeal Dodd-Frank Section 1071, which requires lenders to collect data on loans to small businesses.
quote: Repeal Dodd–Frank Section 1071. This section, which relates to small-business data collection, imposes requirements on financial institutions' lending to small firms

title: Bar CFPB enforcement not based on formal rules
proposal: The chapter says Congress should forbid the CFPB from spending money on enforcement actions that are not based on a rule made through the Administrative Procedure Act process.
quote: Require that no CFPB funds are spent on enforcement actions that are not based on a rulemaking that complies with the Administrative Procedure Act.

title: Let CFPB defendants choose a federal court
proposal: The chapter says people facing CFPB administrative actions should be able to choose whether their case is heard by an administrative law judge or a regular federal court.
quote: Require that respondents in administrative actions be allowed to elect whether an adjudication occurs in an administrative law court or an ordinary Article III federal court.

title: Define "unfair, deceptive, and abusive" practices in law
proposal: The chapter says Congress should spell out what counts as "deceptive, unfair, and abusive" practices to narrow the CFPB's mission more precisely.
quote: Specify the nature of "deceptive, unfair, and abusive" practices to define the scope of the CFPB mission more precisely.
